content: I’m just going to come right out and say it. I love the approach Apple has taken with the HomeView. I think it’s the shared, always-available household interface that my family might finally use. Is Apple’s first smart display my dream smart home dashboard? No. But is it the right product for Apple Home at this moment? Absolutely. A lot of initial reactions to the $299 HomeView (which looks like a giant Apple Watch on a flatter metallic HomePod Mini) ask why you would want it when you can do most of what it offers on your iPhone or iPad. And yes, its features replicate many of the things you already do on the devices you use all the time. But that’s kind of the point. HomeView gives you another interface for those things, but crucially one that is always powered, always unlocked, and always in the same spot in your home, making it easy to walk up to and interact with. I’ve tried using an iPad to control my smart home, run my family’s calendar, and be a shared device for controlling music. It wasn’t great. I’ll have to test HomeView, of course, but my initial impression is that this could be a much better solution for those use cases. [Image: My iPad in the wall experiment lasted several unsuccessful years. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_1308.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] Most iPads are more expensive, have worse speakers, and do not like to be plugged in all the time (I present my sad, warped iPad Mini as tribute). An iPad can’t be a hub for your Apple Home; HomeView can. An iPad famously isn’t a good multiuser device, and controlling home devices on one requires it staying logged in to your personal iCloud account; HomeView offers Apple’s first crack at easy multiuser switching. Apple designed HomeView as a communal device that sits in a fixed place in the home. This means it’s always where you expect it to be, which matters when you want to adjust the thermostat or can’t find your phone and want to check your calendar. Not having a battery or detachable screen is a feature for me, because devices that do inevitably wander off and die under a couch cushion. And while many people are fine using their personal phones and tablets to interact with the digital world when at home, and don’t want yet another device with a screen on their countertop or wall, the millions of Echo Shows, Google Nest Hubs, Skylight Calendars, and the like in homes today are a good indicator that there’s interest in this type of interface. [Image: The HomeView’s footprint is smaller than that of most smart displays I’ve tested. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6046.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] As Apple’s uncharacteristically chaotic launch video shows, HomeView targets a new demographic for the company: busy, Apple-centric households. One feature I’m most interested in is HomeView’s role as a home video phone. Do you know how many times I’ve tried to call my daughter when I’m not home, and her phone is dead or on silent? Based on Apple’s video, if she’s home, my call can now ring on the HomeView. I’ve occasionally used the drop-in feature on Echo smart speakers to get her attention, further proof of the advantage of always-on home devices. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0420_still-2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0420_still.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I see HomeView as filling the awkward space where families don’t want phones at the dinner table or on the kitchen counter, but still want to check what time Zoey’s soccer game is or look up the origin of French toast (yeah, just kidding). This inevitably ends with one person pulling out their phone, which gives everyone else implicit permission to do the same. Smart displays and speakers from Amazon and Google already help with this to some extent, but Apple’s version comes without ads (see the Echo Show) and may have a longer lifespan (RIP Pixel Tablet). Siri AI’s much-hyped “personal context” capabilities, in which it can scan your text messages and emails and serve up relevant information to up to six members of your household, also give it an edge here. [Image: The HomeView has a variety of customizable faces. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6068.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] I asked Kaiann Drance, vice president of product marketing for home at Apple, why Apple chose now for its biggest smart home push yet. She said Siri AI and the personal context it brings, which she called Apple’s “privacy story,” came together with a device designed specifically for the home. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” she said. "As the Siri AI capabilities continue to evolve, the home experience is fitting to be able to interact with in a natural way.”" - Lilian Rincon, Apple Siri AI made this possible because it’s “much more capable,” said Lilian Rincon, vice president of product marketing for AI at Apple. She also pointed to its new conversational abilities. “It’s great because you can just ask it to change the temperature on your thermostat in a very natural way. As the Siri AI capabilities continue to evolve, the home experience is fitting to be able to interact with in this natural way.” On why now, Rincon says the natural-language shift is the point where AI goes mainstream. “Because now it can be … my mother-in-law or the Gen Z who’s in college, both of them can use this in the way that they naturally speak and get what they want.” Siri AI in the home has another big advantage over the competition: It doesn’t say too much. Based on the demos I saw, and my time using Siri AI on the iPhone, when you ask it to do something, it does it without peppering you with follow-up questions. chineseTitle: Apple HomeView 的最大特点可能是它的简单性
chineseSummary: 我只是要直接说出来。我喜欢 Apple 在 HomeView 上采取的方法。我认为这是我的家人最终可能使用的共享的、始终可用的家庭界面。苹果的首款智能显示屏是我梦想的智能家居仪表板吗？不。但它是否适合 Apple Home [...]
chineseContent: 我只想直接说出来。我喜欢 Apple 在 HomeView 上采取的方法。我认为这是我的家人最终可能使用的共享的、始终可用的家庭界面。苹果的首款智能显示屏是我梦想中的智能家居仪表板吗？不。但目前它适合 Apple Home 吗？绝对地。很多人对售价 299 美元的 HomeView（它看起来就像一个巨大的 Apple Watch 搭配一个扁平的金属 HomePod Mini）的最初反应是问，既然你可以在 iPhone 或 iPad 上完成它提供的大部分功能，为什么你会想要它呢？是的，它的功能复制了您在一直使用的设备上已经做的许多事情。但这就是重点。 HomeView 为您提供了处理这些事情的另一种界面，但最重要的是，它始终处于通电状态，始终处于解锁状态，并且始终处于家中的同一位置，从而使您可以轻松走近并与之交互。我尝试过使用 iPad 来控制我的智能家居、运行家人的日历以及作为控制音乐的共享设备。这不太好。当然，我必须测试 HomeView，但我的初步印象是，对于这些用例来说，这可能是一个更好的解决方案。 [图片：我的 iPad 挂在墙上的实验持续了几年，但并不成功。 https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_1308.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] 大多数 iPad 都更贵，扬声器更差，而且不喜欢一直插着电源（我将我悲伤、扭曲的 iPad Mini 作为致敬）。 iPad 不能成为 Apple Home 的中心；主页视图可以。众所周知，iPad 并不是一款优秀的多用户设备，在 iPad 上控制家庭设备需要它保持登录到您的个人 iCloud 帐户； HomeView 为 Apple 提供了第一个轻松实现多用户切换的解决方案。 Apple 将 HomeView 设计为一款位于我身边的公共设备
